target.title: fix(gateway): stop reports success without stopping a foreground gateway
target.body:
Closes #72948

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators stopping a foreground-launched gateway would see
`Gateway service disabled.` with exit code 0 while the gateway kept running and holding
its port.

`openclaw gateway stop` falls back to unmanaged listener discovery when no service manager
owns the gateway, and that discovery shells out to `lsof`. Minimal containers — the norm
for sandboxed runtimes without systemd — do not ship `lsof`, so discovery returns nothing
and stop reports success without signalling anything. The reporter had to fall back to
`kill -TERM <pid>` inside the sandbox. The same false success appears whenever the gateway
runs on a port other than the configured one, because stop scans the configured port.

With `--json`, callers get `"ok": true, "result": "not-loaded"`, so scripts treat the
gateway as stopped when it is still serving.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway lock already records the verified owner pid and port. Restart learned to read
the lock port in #105241 to keep an unmanaged restart honest when the configured port
drifts; stop's fallback still resolved its port from config and found pids through `lsof`
only. This closes that gap instead of adding a second discovery mechanism, and matches the
reporter's own first suggestion ("Read the gateway's lock file").

`runDaemonStop`'s not-loaded fallback now reads the lock identity once and uses its port
for listener discovery and its pid as the signal target when discovery finds no listener.
When verified listeners are found, signalling and output are exactly as before. Resolving
the port from the lock is what also covers the port-override case — the same fix, not a
second one.

Safety comes from existing helpers rather than new checks, in two stages.
`readActiveGatewayLockIdentity` rejects a dead pid outright; if the lock recorded a process
start time and it can be read, it requires an exact match, which is what catches pid
recycling; otherwise it falls back to an argv check. Port-less and non-gateway locks are
rejected. Then `signalVerifiedGatewayPidSync` re-reads argv immediately before `SIGTERM`
and refuses anything that is not a gateway process. The second stage checks argv only, so
it is the guard against signalling an unrelated process rather than a second start-identity
check.

Design note: a lock that exists but cannot be verified is deliberately not turned into an
error. `readActiveGatewayLockIdentity` collapses "no lock", "stale lock" and "port-less
lock" into a single `undefined`, so the caller cannot distinguish them without widening
`gateway-lock.ts`, and the common case — a stale lock left by a crashed gateway while
nothing is running — is correctly reported as not-loaded today. Failing there would turn a
correct no-op into a non-zero exit.

**Known limitation:** when neither a listener nor a verifiable lock owner is found, stop
still prints `Gateway service disabled.`, which reads as "stopped" even though nothing was
signalled. Making that wording honest belongs to the shared `lifecycle-core` not-loaded
path and is out of scope here.

Non-goals: no replacement for `lsof`-based discovery, no change to the `--force`
non-interactive guard or the Linux disabled-unit path, no new config, and no change to
restart.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway stop` now stops a foreground gateway on hosts without `lsof`, and when
the gateway runs on an overridden port, instead of reporting success and leaving it
serving. Automation reading `--json` gets `"result": "stopped"` with the pid signalled.

Scope note: the non-interactive guard added in #110323 means callers that do not pass
`--force` already fail loudly before reaching this fallback. The false success is
reachable for interactive operators and for non-interactive callers that pass `--force`.
The original report predates that guard; the underlying inability to find and stop the
gateway is unchanged, which is what this fixes.

## Evidence

Full-real proof against base `104691f822`: production entry
(`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`), a real foreground gateway, real lock files, real
`SIGTERM`, no mocks. Isolated `HOME`, state dir and port. The no-`lsof` host is reproduced
with a mount namespace masking `/usr/bin/lsof`.

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| No `lsof`, gateway on configured port | `ok:true` `result:"not-loaded"` exit 0, gateway still serving | `ok:true` `result:"stopped"`, process gone, port free |
| `lsof` available, gateway on 39471 while config says 39470 | `ok:true` `result:"not-loaded"` exit 0, gateway still serving | `ok:true` `result:"stopped"` on the lock port, process gone |
| `lsof` available, ports match (existing path) | stops | stops, message unchanged |
| Stale lock from a crashed gateway, nothing running | `not-loaded` exit 0 | `not-loaded` exit 0, nothing signalled |
| Non-interactive without `--force` | guard fails, exit 1 | unchanged |

After, no `lsof` — the gateway that previously survived now shuts down:

```
{ "action": "stop", "ok": true, "result": "stopped",
  "message": "Gateway stop signal sent to unmanaged process on port 39470: <pid>." }

[gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 3350ms
```

Focused tests: `src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.test.ts`, 40/40. Reverting the production
change while keeping the tests fails exactly the two new behavioral cases:

```
× stops the locked gateway owner when listener discovery finds nothing
× stops the active lock port when the configured port has drifted
  Tests  2 failed | 38 passed (40)
```

Credit: mayank6136 reported #72948 with the sandbox reproduction and the manual
`kill -TERM` workaround. #72224 (myagizmaktav) is open against the same `lsof` dependency
but takes a different direction — a new `/proc`-based discovery path, and restart rather
than stop.
